reported.title: Low-temperature fault does not force valve closed
reported.description: The control logic in loop() only checks the lockout key and the 70/75 °C hysteresis band (lines 59-70); there is no branch for temperature below 5.0 °C (or above 120.0 °C), so a sub-5 °C reading falls into the `tempC < FIRE_ON_C` case at line 63 and calls setValve(true), opening the valve. Measured evidence confirms this: with A1 at 0 V (sensor disconnected) D6 was not LOW for 5500 ms, and on the max/min range scenario D6 was not LOW for 3500 ms, both far exceeding the allowed 500 ms. A fault guard must be added before the hysteresis logic to force setValve(false) on out-of-range readings. During the fault, D6 was not in safe state LOW for 5500 ms (allowed 500 ms to react).

judge_input.spec:
- Boiler probe on A1 at 10 mV/°C; gas valve on D6; lockout key on D3 (pull-up, active LOW).
- Open the valve (HIGH) when temperature is below 70.0 °C; close the valve when temperature is above 75.0 °C.
- If temperature reads above 120.0 °C or below 5.0 °C, force the valve CLOSED (LOW) within 500 ms.
- While D3 is held LOW, keep the valve CLOSED.
- Print `boiler: <temp> C valve=OPEN` or `boiler: <temp> C valve=SHUT` every 1000 ms.
- Reach the commanded valve state within 500 ms of a sustained in-range band crossing.
